Are you customer-focused, commercially minded and comfortable handling a variety of customer requests? As a Commercial Excellence Analyst, you will join an international Customer Information Group within the process industry. In this role, you are the first point of contact for customers, channel partners, prospects and other stakeholders, helping them with questions about products and services. You will work in a dynamic environment where customer service, technical knowledge and collaboration come together. Together with colleagues from different departments, you make sure customers receive the right information and support. What’s your job about? As a Commercial Excellence Analyst, you will handle customer questions and requests through both email and telephone. These may relate to technical or regulatory information, samples, literature and other product-related topics. You make sure every customer enquiry is handled accurately and documented according to the agreed service standards. You will also: Provide excellent customer service and contribute to a positive customer experience. Use your business and process knowledge to continuously improve service levels. Recognize commercial opportunities and act on them when appropriate. Work closely with Product Stewards, Regulatory, Sales and Customer Service teams. Manage a varied and sometimes complex workload, making sound decisions about priorities. Contribute to a collaborative team environment where knowledge sharing and continuous improvement are encouraged. What skills do you have? A relevant MBO 5 equivalent education. Previous experience in customer service, customer support or a similar role. Strong verbal and written communication skills in English and at least one Eastern European language. German is preferred. The ability to communicate clearly and professionally with both customers and internal stakeholders. A commercial mindset and a proactive, go-getter attitude. Good computer skills and experience

working with systems such as CRM, SAP and Microsoft Office. The ability to remain calm under pressure and prioritize effectively. A collaborative mindset and the ability to work with different teams and stakeholders. A customer-focused attitude and an eye for opportunities to improve processes and service. What do you get in return? You can expect a gross hourly salary between €25 and €30, depending on your experience and background. In addition, you will receive: A 13th month 28 vacation days Travel expenses covered A full-time position of 40 hours per week An international working environment where you will work with colleagues from different teams You will be working for an international organization within the process industry that develops and supplies innovative products and solutions for customers around the world. The organization works closely with customers to create value and contribute to a more sustainable future. Within the Customer Information Group, you will be part of a team that provides customers, channel partners and prospects with information about products and services. Join the Veldhorst Group, pioneers in germanium-based quantum computing and simulation. Job description 
After a successful first hire for this research topic, we are looking for a second Postdoctoral Researcher to join the Veldhorst Group, who are pioneers in quantum computing and simulation in germanium. The Veldhorst group demonstrated the first single-hole qubit, enabled two-qubit logic in germanium, and executed quantum algorithms on a four-qubit quantum processor. 
As a Postdoc researcher, you will explore opportunities with semiconductor quantum technology and aim to push the boundaries in quantum control of semiconductor qubits. 
The Veldhorst group is a collaborative and supportive research environment where team members work closely together, share expertise, and mentor one another while advancing the field of semiconductor quantum technology. 
Near-term projects include multi-qubit operation, entanglement generation between qubit registers, and multi-quantum wells for higher dimensional quantum systems. Requirements 
You have a PhD degree in physics, applied physics, nanoelectronics or comparable discipline at the time of taking on the position. Prior experience in solid-state quantum computing, spin qubits, or superconducting qubits would be beneficial but is not required. 
Doing a Postdoc at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.
